entries.title: France, UK and Spain see record temperatures as heatwave grips western Europe
entries.snippet: Tens of millions of people are grappling with punishing temperatures, which have led to red heat alerts across the continent.

entries.title: Air conditioning creates political divide after France records hottest day
entries.snippet: France is being forced to re-think its longstanding reservations about air-conditioning as temperatures soar.

entries.title: UN nuclear chief says inspectors will visit Iran sites as part of war deal
entries.snippet: Rafael Grossi says the IAEA is "working on modalities" but an Iranian minister says such access would only be part of a final deal with the US.

entries.title: Clean sweep for Mamdani-backed candidates in New York's Democratic primary
entries.snippet: Brad Lander unseats Dan Goldman in a race that laid bare the city's divisions over the Israel-Gaza war.

entries.title: Biggest city in Crimea without power after Ukraine strikes
entries.snippet: Sevastopol's Moscow-installed governor warns there will be no electricity in some areas until the evening.

entries.title: France confirms first Ebola case
entries.snippet: The French doctor had been working in DR Congo, where more than 260 people are known to have died.

entries.title: French woman allegedly held captive by husband for 12 years rescued in Pakistan
entries.snippet: Yasmina alleges she was held along with her five children, and they were all cut off from the outside world.

entries.title: Colombia's left-wing presidential candidate concedes defeat
entries.snippet: Senator Iván Cepeda was beaten by right-wing businessman Abelardo de la Espriella by less than a percentage point.

entries.title: Sydney woman wakes from induced coma more than a week after shark attack
entries.snippet: Leah Stewart, 34, had one of her arms amputated after she was bitten while swimming at Coogee Beach.

entries.title: Eight sentenced to 450 years in prison over anti-ICE riot where officer was shot
entries.snippet: An officer was shot in the neck during the Texas disorder by "Antifa Cell operatives", prosecutors said.

entries.title: Bondi Beach shooting hero pleads not guilty to alleged assault on his father
entries.snippet: Ahmed al Ahmed tackled one of the gunmen who killed 15 people at a Jewish event in December.

entries.title: Kenya to charge students with murder over deadly school fire
entries.snippet: Sixteen pupils, aged between 15 and 18, died when a fire broke out in a dormitory at Utumishi Girls' School last month.

entries.title: Congress passes war powers measure for first time, breaking with Trump over Iran
entries.snippet: Experts say Trump is likely to ignore it, but that even though it carries little power, it is politically significant.

entries.title: Dozens of ships head through Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran deal
entries.snippet: Traffic in the waterway has risen since the US and Iran signed a deal aimed at ending the war, including 42 ships on Saturday alone.

entries.title: Germany rail network briefly halted nationwide due to IT malfunction
entries.snippet: Rail company Deutsche Bahn had to pause train services across the country for more than two-and-a-half hours.

entries.title: Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba sues US government over defence blacklist
entries.snippet: It is suing the US defence department after it was added to a list of firms with ties to the Chinese military.

entries.title: Stanford graduates rethink their futures as AI transforms tech
entries.snippet: The BBC spoke with Stanford University graduates about what they really think about artificial intelligence.

entries.title: Blood ties and opportunity: Why more World Cup players than ever are not representing their birth nations
entries.snippet: Nearly a quarter of footballers at the 2026 tournament are not playing for their country of birth.

entries.title: From startups to global spotlight - Indian entrepreneur takes charge of WhatsApp
entries.snippet: Kunal Shah has been a recognisable figure in India's startup ecosystem for a while but now he faces global spotlight.

entries.title: Why are there holiday delay warnings over the EU's new border system?
entries.snippet: The EU's much-delayed Entry/Exit System will change the way UK passengers travel to 29 countries.

entries.title: Meta plans to release AI-powered prediction market app, documents show
entries.snippet: The company is building an app separate from Facebook and Instagram where people can wager on the outcome of real-world events, using "play money."

entries.title: A judge says the Kennedy Center must update him on its plans — and address that tarp
entries.snippet: A federal judge has ordered the Kennedy Center to update him on programming and operational plans. But with most of the staff gone and many artists booked elsewhere, what shows would they present?

entries.title: Postal Service says its cash crisis is delayed until at least 2031, but problems loom
entries.snippet: The U.S. Postal Service is no longer set to be out of cash in 2027, the agency's head says. But its finances remain shaky as Trump officials keep putting it in political hot water.

entries.title: Will Texas' new top voting official be a 'disruptor'? Locals are preparing for it
entries.snippet: Just ahead of closely contested midterms, Texas is about to get a new top voting official. Many locals there fear the frontrunner is a state lawmaker and pastor with no election experience.

entries.title: Understanding 'masculinism,' a movement to restore the primacy of men
entries.snippet: Masculinism is a belief that feminism emasculates men, and men should be in control while women stay at home raising children. The Atlantic writer Helen Lewis says the movement is becoming mainstream.

entries.title: US eases restriction on Iran's World Cup team, allowing travel 2 days before next match
entries.snippet: The U.S. is easing its restrictions on Iran's World Cup team. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said Tuesday the squad could travel into the country two days before its next match.

entries.title: Star Fox Review: Can't quite teach an old Fox new tricks
entries.snippet: The Switch 2 Star Fox remake comes with high-effort visuals and a fun battle mode, but its campaign feels stuck in the past.

entries.title: Greetings from sweltering Switzerland
entries.snippet: On the waterfront in Lucerne, Switzerland, soccer fans watched jumbo TVs showing a World Cup match played an ocean away. But the air felt more like the tropics.

entries.title: U.N. nuclear chief says inspectors will visit Iran, but Iran says only after final deal
entries.snippet: The head of the U.N.'s atomic agency said Iran's nuclear enrichment sites would be inspected as part of the interim deal. Iran insists any such visit would only come after a final deal.

entries.title: Congress passes major housing bill. And, Mamdani-backed candidates sweep NYC primaries
entries.snippet: Congress has passed the largest housing affordability bill in decades. And all three candidates endorsed by New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani have won their primaries.

entries.title: WATCH: Under proposed rule, USPS won't deliver mail ballots to states that don't provide voter rolls, postmaster general says
entries.snippet: Postmaster General David Steiner told a Senate committee Wednesday that, if a proposed rule is adopted, the U.S. Postal Service would withhold mail ballots from states that do not hand over to the federal government lists of people who have requested absentee or mail ballots.

entries.title: Trump scraps housing bill signing to pressure Senate GOP on SAVE Act

entries.title: Progressive victories signal mood of some Democratic voters ahead of midterms
entries.snippet: Progressive Democrats dominated New York's midterm primary elections in a resounding show of strength for the Democratic Socialist mayor of New York City. All three candidates endorsed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani won their races, two of them ousting sitting congressmen. Geoff Bennett

entries.title: How the Trump administration is trying to reshape how elections are run
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has made multiple efforts to reshape how elections are run with just months before the midterms. The debate over election security has led to tension between the White House and election administrators as the president falsely claims voter fraud is rampan

entries.title: News Wrap: During Gulf nations tour, Rubio stresses Strait of Hormuz must remain open

entries.title: Another top military commander resigns following clash with Hegseth
entries.snippet: The Army confirmed that one of its most prominent generals would soon be retiring, ending his career and leaving his current job long before expected. It is the latest example of senior officers leaving the military early, or being fired, under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Nic

entries.title: Millions in Europe face extreme temperatures from record-breaking heat wave
entries.snippet: A major heat wave is shattering records across Europe, leaving tens of millions of people under sweltering conditions. France topped a record for the country's hottest day ever for the second consecutive day. The United Kingdom and Spain both hit record highs for the month of Jun

entries.title: Anti-ICE protesters sentenced to decades in prison in latest crackdown on dissent
entries.snippet: In two federal courts, a group of protesters received unusually long sentences after the Justice Department accused them of being members of Antifa. These nine protesters were arrested after they demonstrated outside a migrant detention facility in Texas. During the protest, a po

entries.title: Walter Isaacson on what he calls 'The Greatest Sentence Ever Written'
entries.snippet: Ahead of America's 250th anniversary, author Walter Isaacson has turned his attention to a single sentence in the Declaration of Independence. Judy Woodruff spoke with Isaacson about the enduring power of those words and his new book, "The Greatest Sentence Ever Written." It's pa

entries.title: White House seeks $87.6B from Congress for Iran war costs, U.S. farmers and Ebola response
entries.snippet: The White House has formally requested $87.6 billion mostly to replenish the Pentagon after the U.S. war against Iran, submitting the request to Congress at a politically difficult time as Republican and Democratic lawmakers have objected to any further military action.

entries.title: WATCH: Congress dedicates national time capsule ahead of America's 250th anniversary
entries.snippet: The Time Capsule Act, a 2016 law creating the nonpartisan America250 commission mandated that a time capsule be buried in Philadelphia on July 4, 2026, and dug up 250 years later in 2276.

entries.title: Kennedy scion Jack Schlossberg loses crowded New York City congressional primary
entries.snippet: Kennedy family scion and political novice Jack Schlossberg lost Tuesday to New York state Assembly Member Micah Lasher, in a closely watched and crowded Democratic primary for an open congressional seat in the heart of Manhattan.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump meets with NATO Secretary-General Rutte in the Oval Office
entries.snippet: Trump has renewed his threats to leave the alliance, raising the stakes before the NATO leaders' summit in Turkey next month. But Rutte, who has become known as a Trump whisperer for his ability to charm the president, was looking to appease him Wednesday.

entries.title: A member of the cultlike Zizians group is charged in the killings of her parents in Pennsylvania
entries.snippet: Michelle Zajko, who has been jailed in Maryland on other charges since February 2025, has been charged with murder, burglary and conspiracy charges in the deaths of Rita and Richard Zajko, Delaware County District Attorney Tanner Rouse said at a news conference.

entries.title: Ex-aides win primaries to replace retiring Democratic House members
entries.snippet: U.S. Reps. Steny Hoyer and Jerrold Nadler passed the torch Tuesday night to former aides who won the Democratic primaries to replace them on Capitol Hill.

entries.title: Former NYC Mayor Adams' chief of staff and 3 others charged in federal bribery probe
entries.snippet: A former chief of staff to ex-New York Mayor Eric Adams was arrested Wednesday in a bribery case, the latest sign that federal prosecutors continue to scrutinize Adams' inner circle months after the scandal-bruised Democrat left office.

entries.title: How a heat dome is formed and why experts blame one for Europe's baking temperatures
entries.snippet: Europe is sizzling under an early heat wave this week, with millions of people experiencing extremely high temperatures, and experts say a phenomenon known as a heat dome is to blame.

entries.title: Dispute over nuclear inspections shows how U.S. and Iran are negotiating in public
entries.snippet: The head of the U.N.'s nuclear agency said Wednesday that Iranian nuclear enrichment sites would be visited by his inspectors as part of the interim U.S.-Iran deal to reach an end to the war. An Iranian diplomat instead insisted any such visit would only come after a final deal.

entries.title: Federal judge bars Trump from implementing proof of citizenship requirement to vote
entries.snippet: The ruling by U.S. District Court Judge Denise Casper in Boston effectively converts a preliminary injunction she issued a year ago, in which she temporarily blocked many of Trump's efforts to overhaul elections, into a permanent ban.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Venezuela hit by two powerful earthquakes
entries.snippet: Strong earthquakes struck west of Venezuela's capital just seconds apart, bringing down buildings in Caracas.

entries.title: Germany's Merz rallies European NATO allies ahead of summit
entries.snippet: Chancellor Friedrich Merz hosted leaders of European NATO powers in Berlin to hash out consensus on bolstering European defense. With US tensions looming, the leaders signaled that transatlantic ties are improving.

entries.title: What does British PM's resignation mean for European security?
entries.snippet: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer was widely known for his support of Ukraine and his efforts towards a new EU–UK defense partnership. What will happen to those policies now that Starmer has announced his resignation?

entries.title: How Big Tech is changing journalism
entries.snippet: Technology companies are shaping how news is presented and digested, leaving media outlets little option but to comply. At DW's Global Media Forum in Bonn, participants discussed how to resist and adapt.

entries.title: Heat wave: Why you should skip that cold beer or cocktail
entries.snippet: Summer, the FIFA World Cup and a cold beer. Sounds like a dream? Be careful, though; the combination of heat and alcohol can quickly take a very bad turn.

entries.title: European heat wave is not normal summer weather
entries.snippet: Human-induced climate change has intensified temperatures, making this year's record heat wave up to 4 degrees Celsius hotter.

entries.title: Iran after the war — fragile peace, shattered economy
entries.snippet: The US has temporarily allowed Iran to export oil and indicated it will provide billions to relieve the crisis triggered by the war. With ordinary Iranians at their limit, however, Tehran already fears new protests.

entries.title: Climate change: Heatwave costs the German economy billions
entries.snippet: Never before has a June been as hot in Germany as in 2026. This has consequences not only for people and nature, but also for businesses. Heat reduces productivity and causes illness, while cooling is expensive.

entries.title: France reports first Congo outbreak linked Ebola case
entries.snippet: France has confirmed its first Ebola case linked to the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The infection comes weeks after European health authorities said there were no active Ebola cases in the EU.

entries.title: Is xenophobia in South Africa risking investment?
entries.snippet: Vigilante groups and right-wing populist forces are stoking anti-immigrant sentiment and demanding that they leave the country by June 30. Experts fear serious economic implications for the country and the region.

entries.title: Southeast Asia boost defense ties but avoids firm alliances
entries.snippet: Countries across the region are expanding defense cooperation in ways that change the South China Sea equation but fall short of a new anti-China bloc.

entries.title: Trump offers Iran an economic lifeline — with strings
entries.snippet: Iran has seen a speedy rebound in oil exports after the US-Iran deal granted immediate waivers on US sanctions. Relief on frozen assets and a $300 billion reconstruction fund now hinge on Tehran meeting key conditions.

entries.title: North Korean soldier crosses border to South
entries.snippet: South Korea's military says it is investigating the soldier's reasons for crossing the inner-Korean border. While dozens of North Koreans flee each year, usually via China, crossing directly south is very rare.

entries.title: India news: Protests in northern region Ladakh over talks with Delhi
entries.snippet: Businesses in both northern Leh and Kargil districts remained shut to protest the alleged retraction of key constitutional and administrative agreements. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: China detains two Japanese nationals on smuggling charges
entries.snippet: China has detained two Japanese nationals on suspicion of smuggling banned goods. Reports suggest that at least one case may involve strategic rare-earth-related exports.

entries.title: World Cup: Why Mexico may be LA's favorite team
entries.snippet: Mexican-American football fans in the USA often split allegiances between their two cultures. For many in Los Angeles, the Mexico national team trumps the nation they call home.

entries.title: Iran nuclear inspections 'going to happen,' says IAEA head
entries.snippet: After contradicting US and Iranian statements, the UN nuclear agency said inspections of Iran's nuclear sites would take place. Iran's top negotiator called the US-Iran deal "America's declaration of defeat." More at DW.

entries.title: Why Austrian author Ingeborg Bachmann remains a literary icon
entries.snippet: A new documentary featuring Sandra Hüller celebrates the Austrian poet and author who was a literary star of her era. She would have turned 100 this year.

entries.title: How Africa's youth wants to save democracy
entries.snippet: Africa's young population often finds itself facing aging, autocratic rulers. Unwilling to settle for democratic rituals alone, many are searching for creative new ways to shape their future.
